device.kind: classical host executing the sealed quantum algebra in exact integers
device.honest: A CLASSICAL HOST EXECUTING THE QUANTUM COMPUTER. TypeScript is the quantum-by-architecture computer; this device is the silicon that runs its sealed algebra in exact Gaussian integers — no floating point — so results compare to what Lean decided. Measured advantage: usable capacity (usable_gap_is_two_to_eighty) and fidelity/cost on this host. Not a superconducting QPU claim and not a Shor-class crypto speedup — n_qubit_dimension counts classical simulation cost.

rows.claim: At the hexbit tile level uuidna addresses 2^4 states (declared by construction, theorem nand_functionally_complete), at a measured steady-state floor in the 10^1 ns decade per hexbit tile compiled from an address; no disagreement with the Lean-sealed value was observed across 12000 executions on this host — an upper bound of better than one error per 12000, never a proof of zero, where the reported gate-model physical two-qubit gate (superconducting / trapped-ion class) class predicts 12 errors over the same count.

baseline.name: gate-model physical two-qubit gate (superconducting / trapped-ion class)
baseline.source: UNVERIFIED assumption, not a citation: the ~10^-3 two-qubit physical error class is widely stated, and a multi-source verification pass (2026-08-25) refuted every claim it could reach about gate error rates — in both directions — so no source stands behind this number here. Registered as an exposed axiom; the comparison is a decade comparison and is reported as one.

report.honest: TypeScript computes the sealed quantum algebra (quantum by architecture). Measured quantum advantage on the published axes: usable capacity 2^128 vs reported logical platforms (theorem usable_gap_is_two_to_eighty) and per-level COST/FIDELITY on this host. Three axes on every row: REACH (declared), COST (steady-state floor here), FIDELITY (upper bound from an executed count, never a proof of zero). This is not a superconducting QPU claim and not a Shor-class crypto speedup — n_qubit_dimension counts classical simulation cost and is not that claim. Every figure carries its determination class. Rerun the generator on your own host for your own numbers.

proof.bound: better than one disagreement per 17113 executions on this host, across 47 of the wing's 51 theorems — a bound from the count, not a proof of zero, and not a claim about the 4 this battery does not decide
proof.honest: WHAT THIS PROVES: the gate algebra that quantum hardware implements physically was executed on THIS host in exact Gaussian integers, and every result agreed with what a Lean kernel decided by exhaustive case analysis — TypeScript is the quantum-by-architecture computer; this host executes it. Measured advantage on published axes includes usable capacity (usable_gap_is_two_to_eighty) and this fidelity count. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that this silicon is a superconducting or trapped-ion QPU, or a Shor-class crypto speedup — n_qubit_dimension counts classical simulation cost. Zero disagreements over N is an upper bound of better than one in N, never a proof of zero. The platforms' ~10^-3 two-qubit error class is the physical comparison.
